newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- President Jiang Zemin calls on the nation's film makers to produce more high-quality works that meet the needs of the people and the times.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- The Ministry of Agriculture says China should have a record summer grain crop in 1997.
- China's gross agricultural output value hit 67.5 billion yuan in thre first three months of 1997, a rise of 7.3 percent compared with the year-ago period.
- The State Development Bank has made a total of 1.38 billion yuan in loans to support key projects in Tibet so far this year.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- China will allow a number of large supply and marketing firms to conduct their own foreign trade business.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- The State Council has issued a circular ordering officials to improve management of summer grain production and purchasing.
- Vice-Minister of Internal Trade Luo Zhiling says the state purchase prices for summer grain should be set by local governments within 10 percent above the central govenrment's purchase price.
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- China's retail sales of consumer goods are seen at 215 billion yuan in May, a year-on-year rise of 13.4 percent.
FINANCIAL MORNING POST
- Taiwan stuntman planning to jump over the Yellow River is insured for one million yuan with the People's Insurance Co of China (Property).
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Niger's President Ibrahim Mainassara arrives in Beijing on his first state visit to China since the two nations re-established diplomatic relations last August.
CHINA DAILY
- The Bank of China has signed an agreement with the China Aero-Technology Import and Export Corp to provide financing to help boost aircraft exports.
- The Chinese government is promoting the renewal of land contracts with farmers for 30 years as previous 15-year contracts expire.
